Teledyne e2v adds Perciva ToF to its 3D imaging range

The new industrial depth camera combines a Hydra3D+ sensor and onboard processing for robotics, logistics and inspection.

RoboticsTomorrow ↗15 September 2026English editorial summary
Story

Industrial depth sensing

Teledyne e2v introduced Perciva ToF for applications that need depth information, including logistics, robotics and inspection. The camera brings the sensor and processing together in a single device.

The Hydra3D+ sensor

Perciva uses an 832 × 600-pixel Hydra3D+ CMOS sensor with HiRho technology. The manufacturer says its pixel design supports near-infrared sensitivity and low-reflectivity materials while reducing imaging problems with fast-moving objects.

Ready-to-use data over GigE

Factory calibration and onboard processing allow the camera to deliver depth maps and 3D point clouds directly over GigE. This is intended to simplify integration for developers and system integrators.

Demonstrations and supporting information

The announcement says Teledyne plans to demonstrate the camera at VISION in Stuttgart on 6–8 October 2026 and offers documentation or product samples on request. The performance statements are manufacturer claims rather than independent tests in this report.
